skill.name: alphafold-database
skill.description: Access AlphaFold DB protein structure predictions, download coordinate and confidence files, and interpret pLDDT and PAE metrics for research workflows.
skill.summary: Retrieve AlphaFold predictions and confidence metrics for structural biology workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, public scientific API URLs, SQL identifiers, biological accessions, and expected local data downloads. Confirmed risks remain in an unsafe shell=True subprocess example in SKILL.md and a remote installer piped into bash in references/api_reference.md; no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unsafe shell command construction in the bulk download example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with subprocess.run([...], check=True), validate taxonomy_id, and constrain output_dir to an intended local directory.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell command with official installation documentation or package manager commands that support review and integrity checks.

static_findings.snippet: Always cache downloaded files locally to avoid repeated downloads.
- **Model coordinates** (`model_v4.cif`): Atomic coordinates in mmCIF/PDBx format
- **Predicted Aligned Error** (`predicted_aligned_error_v4.json`): PAE matrix for residue pair confi
**AlphaFold ID:** Internal identifier format: `AF-[UniProt accession]-F[fragment number]` (e.g., "AF
**Database Version:** Current version is v4. File URLs include version suffix (e.g., `model_v4.cif`)
- Cache downloaded files locally to avoid repeated downloads
- Use Biopython for simple single-protein access

content.value_statement: Finding reliable AI-predicted protein structures can take time across several public resources. This skill guides AlphaFold DB lookup, file download, and confidence interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve AlphaFold prediction metadata by UniProt accession.
Build direct download links for mmCIF, PDB, confidence, and PAE files.
Explain pLDDT and PAE confidence metrics for predicted structures.
Show Biopython, requests, BigQuery, and gsutil access patterns.
Guide batch processing and local caching for multiple proteins.
limitations: It depends on external AlphaFold, UniProt, EBI, and Google Cloud services.
It provides guidance and examples, not a bundled client application.
It does not validate biological conclusions or replace experimental structures.
Bulk downloads may require bandwidth, storage, quotas, or cloud setup.

use_cases.title: Retrieve One Protein Structure
use_cases.description: Find the AlphaFold prediction for a known UniProt accession and choose the right coordinate file format.

use_cases.title: Build a Batch Analysis Workflow
use_cases.description: Download multiple predictions, collect confidence scores, and prepare a table for downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Screen Candidate Drug Targets
use_cases.description: Review predicted structures, pLDDT values, and domain confidence before docking or binding site analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to find the AlphaFold prediction for UniProt P00520. Explain which files I should download and why.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Confidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Review confidence metrics for one protein.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how I should interpret pLDDT and PAE for an AlphaFold model of my protein target.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Batch Downloads
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a batch AlphaFold workflow for these UniProt IDs: P00520, P12931, and P04637. Include caching and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Proteome Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a BigQuery strategy for finding high-confidence human AlphaFold predictions suitable for structural comparison.

output_examples.input: Find the AlphaFold model for UniProt P00520.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the AlphaFold entry, lists coordinate and confidence file options, and explains when to use mmCIF or PDB.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a model is reliable for domain analysis.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes pLDDT and PAE interpretation, then separates high-confidence regions from uncertain domain arrangements.

output_examples.input: Plan a batch download for a species proteome.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Google Cloud bulk access, local caching, storage planning, and retry handling for large downloads.

best_practices: Check pLDDT and PAE before using any predicted structure downstream.
Cache downloaded files and record the AlphaFold database version.
Use bulk Google Cloud access for large proteome workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not treat predicted structures as experimental evidence without validation.
Do not ignore low-confidence regions during docking or engineering analysis.
Do not repeatedly download the same large files without caching.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: A UniProt accession is the best starting point. Protein names may need a UniProt lookup first.

faq.question: Can it download complete proteomes?
faq.answer: It explains Google Cloud access patterns for bulk proteome files, but the user must provide storage and bandwidth.

faq.question: Does it validate model quality?
faq.answer: It helps interpret pLDDT and PAE confidence metrics. It does not prove biological correctness.

faq.question: Which file format should I use?
faq.answer: mmCIF is usually best for modern structure workflows. PDB is useful for older tools with format limits.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: Most direct AlphaFold file and API examples are public. Some Google Cloud workflows may require local setup.

faq.question: Can it compare structures?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for retrieving and preparing structures. Comparison depends on external analysis tools.
